text: The Patriots face a critical Week 2 bounce-back opportunity against the Steelers with a depleted secondary, as Carlton Davis III has been downgraded to out after initially being questionable, forcing New England to navigate the cornerback position without its starter while the Steelers simultaneously deal with their own absence in WR Michael Pittman Jr. On the positive side, RB TreVeyon Henderson—who sat out the opener with an ankle injury—declared himself "ready to go" and is expected to return, and the team elevated P Mitch Wishnowsky from the practice squad for the second consecutive week to handle punting duties. The week also brought a poignant moment as Stephon Gilmore, the franchise's 2019 NFL Defensive Player of the Year and two-time All-Pro, signed a one-day contract to retire as a Patriot, cementing his legacy as one of the greatest cornerbacks in New England history. Off the field, owner Robert Kraft explained his decision to remove Macklemore as an opening act for Ed Sheeran's Gillette Stadium shows, citing concerns about the artist's history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery.
